dedupe_keys.name: ibm amlworld realistic synthetic financial transactions for anti money laundering neurips 2023

description: AMLworld is a set of synthetic financial transaction datasets for anti-money laundering research, produced by an agent-based generator calibrated to match real transactions as closely as possible, with complete ground-truth labels for laundering transactions. The paper describes the generator and shows how the datasets can compare machine learning models on detecting laundering patterns that cross banks and national borders. It was written by Erik Altman, Jovan Blanuša, Luc von Niederhäusern, Beni Egressy, Andreea Anghel and Kubilay Atasu and published in the NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Coverage is synthetic and not tied to a country. The datasets are stated to be publicly available free; the proceedings page read offers the paper, supplement and BibTeX, but not the dataset location or licence. Caveats: the data are simulated, so detection results may not transfer to real banks, although labels are complete where real data miss undetected laundering. For simulation it provides benchmark transaction networks for testing graph and agent-based models of payment flows and financial crime detection. It is related to the AMLSim record in this catalogue, IBM's earlier open simulator for synthetic laundering data.
